geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the dominant bar seed with a courtyard operator to transform the paired block into a single public-facing massing rule.
Create a clearer central void and reduce the impression of two solids colliding.
Open the court toward the verified access side to establish an active ground threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing dominant mass into a clearer courtyard-based organizer so the form reads as one primary mass around a public void rather than two colliding volumes.
Increase the carved public void so the street-facing ground response becomes legible and usable.
Align the primary opening to the program's access-side condition and strengthen the public threshold on the verified frontage side in program frame.

rationale: The four views read as a coherent object only weakly: there is a recognizable split-wing / paired-mass gesture, but the form is still too close to two adjacent blocks with a narrow seam rather than one dominant massing idea. The top view suggests the mass responds to the parcel, but the response is not strongly articulated as a public court or active threshold on the verified access edge; the blue frontage is met more as a side condition than as a legible ground response. The silhouette has some section interest, yet it does not become a convincing inhabited terrace or capacity-bearing stepped landform, and the visual relationship between roof, void, and ground is underdeveloped for neighborhood living. Programmatically it is plausible as compact mixed-use/neighborhood massing, but the active ground edge and public void invariants are only partially expressed, so the program-fit hard pass should fail.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/community-center scale and distributed massing than a compact street-building; do not copy the spread-out footprint.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise courtyard composition with connected wings and a legible communal void; good precedent for a neighborhood building with shared open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story hospitality typology is materially lighter than the requested 5-floor neighborhood living mass; only the ground-edge logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple pavilion-like ground response with a clear entry setback and one strong attached vertical/servicing element; useful for active edge and threshold logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: this is a housing megastructure with strong long-span sectional identity; the candidate is far more compact and should not be pushed toward a large continuous terraced superform.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/sectional massing and courtyard orientation can inspire a coherent void-and-ramp relationship.

warnings: Access-edge response appears semantically weak relative to the verified frontage; the ground seam is not yet clearly public.
The mass is close to a generic paired extrusion and risks reading as two colliding solids rather than one resolved spatial rule.
Section does not yet support a strong public terrace or hierarchical ground-to-upper mass transition.
